Commentary.Commentary: That's it then from this game and it is New Zealand who have sealed the three-match T20I series 2-0! There is one more game left and West Indies have a lot to play for in that game. The hosts will try hard to get a win and boost their confidence but the visitors will be eyeing a clean sweep. The third and final T20I will be played on 15 August and it will begin at 12 am IST (6.30 pm GMT, the previous day). Our build-up though will begin much sooner. Do join us then. Cheers!

The Kiwi skipper, Kane Williamson says that it was a fantastic performance from them and they know how potent the opposition is. Adds that they did it with the bat and then to back it with the ball as well was impressive. Adds that they needed to rotate the squad and Michael Bracewell contributed really well to the team. Mentions that T20 cricket can be really fickle in nature and they always try to adapt and the key is to keep it nice and simple, allowing players to settle in. Says that they had a couple of good performances and hopes it will be another one in the next game.

West Indies captain, Nicholas Pooran says that they didn't show up and the opposition batted them out of the game. Adds that they lost early wickets and couldn't build any partnerships. Says that in hindsight, they have just two spinners in the whole squad and ideally they like to play both of them but they didn't bowl well and it is all about discipline. Mentions that they have a chat about it but disappoint on the field. Adds that they felt that they just had to stay in the game and they struggled and were outplayed and they need to accept certain things and keep fighting. Mentions that it is difficult to perform and win every single game but they are a young group of players and they play every other day and is proud of the guys with all the injuries and everything else.

Glenn Phillips (76 off 41 balls) is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his impressive showing with the bat and in the field. Phillips says that coming back to Sabina Park feels great and he has happy memories here, a great feeling to do it for his country. Adds that the Windies bowlers bowled well upfront and took pace off it but it got better for batting later on. Says that it was similar to the wicket from the first game and it's just that they were more clinical this time around. Says that a lot of credit goes to Ramnaresh Sarwan for his performances in the Caribbean and says that they work hard to adapt to different conditions
The Presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the game, Kane Williamson opted to bat first and make use of the batting-friendly conditions. After a stuttering start, Devon Conway and Glenn Phillips took on the Windies bowlers and the scoring rate kept on rising. It was then an 83-run quick-fire stand between Phillips and Daryl Mitchell that took the visitors on course of a score of above 200 runs. The Windies bowlers never really showed much fight and even though a couple of them bowled well, it wasn't enough. During the chase, the Kiwi spinners, Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell both got wickets off their first deliveries and never let their foot off the gas. The Windies had yet another top-order collapse and the runs had to be mustered by those down the order, which was just way too much to do. New Zealand have sealed the T20I series with this impressive win.

The Kiwis were absolutely brilliant. First with the bat and then with the ball. They totally outplayed the hosts and have now taken a 2-0 lead in the series. Phillips and Mitchell were the stars with the bat and the spin twins, Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell were the ones with the ball as they picked up three wickets each and were highly economical.

Yet another defeat for the Windies and quite a big one too. As we said, the stand between Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips batted the Windies out of the game. They needed someone to play a special knock and that did not come. They were 7 down even before they crossed the 100-run mark and from there was, this was never going to be chased. Even though the tailenders got a few lusty blows in but it was just to decrease the margin of defeat. Yet another disappointing show from the hosts.

SIX! Hayden Walsh ends the Windies innings in style but they have fallen well short here. Full and on the pads, Walsh whips it away over the mid-wicket fence for a maximum. New Zealand win by 90 runs!
Back of a length, this is struck down to long off for a single.
Banged in short and at the body, Hayden Walsh gives the charge and pulls it towards mid-wicket for one.

In the air, dropped! Slower delivery, on a length and around off. Obed McCoy mistimes the lofted shot and the ball goes over mid off. James Neesham runs back from the cover region and gets there but ends up spilling it. Single taken.

Just short and great adjustment in the deep from Glenn Phillips to save the boundary. Short of a length and over middle, McCoy pulls it hard and flat to the right of the man at deep mid-wicket. Phillips comes in and then has to quickly switch to his right to keep it out. Two taken.
Southee comes from around the wicket and serves a slower length ball, angling into middle. Obed McCoy backs away and swings across the line but is well beaten.
Quicker one, on leg stump, this is pulled away in front of mid-wicket for just a single.
FOUR LEG BYES! This is poor bowling from Ish Sodhi. Floated up down the leg side and turning further down, McCoy misses the sweep and the ball eludes the keeper, running away into the fine leg fence.
WIDE! Sodhi tries to push it wider but spills it beyond the tramline outside off, wide called.
SIX! MUSCLED! Shorter this time from Sodhi, around middle, McCoy hangs deep and pulls it hard and flat over wide long on for a biggie.

FOUR! Nicely struck and the 100 comes up for West Indies. Fuller and around middle and leg, McCoy gets down on one knee and slogs it away in between long on and deep mid-wicket for a one-bounce boundary.
On a nagging length, sliding it across the left-hander, McCoy goes on the back foot and eases it out on the off side.
This is short and around leg, Walsh pulls it down to deep mid-wicket and rotates the strike.
Very full again and angling at the toes, McCoy backs away and the ball goes between his legs towards the keeper.
Very full and on middle, hit straight to the man at mid off.
Nice change from Boult. The slower bumper now, around off, McCoy steps out and looks to take it on but is comprehensively beaten.
FOUR! Full and around off, Obed McCoy drives through the line of the ball and creams it past the diving extra cover fielder for a boundary.
Length ball, angling into leg stump, McCoy stands tall and looks to go downtown but gets a big inside edge onto the pads.
Boult goes full and attacks the pads, Walsh flicks it away towards fine leg for a single.
FOUR! Edged away! Southee keeps it full and close to the off pole, Obed McCoy looks to drive but gets an outside edge. The ball rolls along the ground and runs away into the third man fence.
Full again, angling into middle and leg. Hayden Walsh backs away and taps it towards mid off for a quick single.
Fuller and around off, Walsh opens the face of the bat and drives it towards short third man.
A touch fuller and closer to the off pole, Walsh has a dab at it but gets beaten past the outside edge.
Good length, outside off and left alone by Hayden Walsh.
Obed McCoy is the last man in for West Indies.

OUT! CAUGHT! Tim Southee gets on the wickets column as West Indies are a wicket away from getting bundled out. This is pitched up on leg stump and the pace is taken off the ball by Southee. Odean Smith backs away and tries to lift it over the mid-wicket fence but gets no timing on it. The ball goes high and towards deep mid-wicket. Glenn Phillips settles under it and takes it a couple of inches off the ground.
Commentary.Howout: c Glenn Phillips b Tim Southee

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter again, this is tapped away towards point for a run.
Quicker and flatter, at the stumps, blocked out.
SIX! Flighted delivery, around off, Odean Smith just frees his arms and lofts it inside-out over the wide long off fence or a maximum.
Hayden Walsh is the new man in.

OUT! TAKEN! Kane Williamson takes a steepler and West Indies lose their eighth wicket. This is tossed up from Mitchell Santner, around off and just allowing it to turn away. Romario Shepherd tries to slog it away but gets a top edge that goes high and over the cover region. Kane Williamson from extra cover paddles back and takes a tumbling catch over his shoulders. Santner gets his third and New Zealand inching closer to victory.
Commentary.Howout: c Kane Williamson b Mitchell Santner

Commentary.Commentary: Swung hard but just for a single. This is quicker and angling into leg stump, Smith ships it away towards deep mid-wicket for one.
Flatter delivery on off, this is played off the back foot and through mid off for a run.
This is very full and at the toes, Shepherd flicks it away to deep square leg for a single.
Top delivery! Boult goes back to bowling over the wicket and nails the yorker on off stump. Romario Shepherd does well to get some bat on it.
This is banged in short and over middle, Smith pulls it down to deep mid-wicket for just a single.
Boult switches to around the wicket and bowls it on a good length, outside off. Odean Smith taps it towards point.
Full and straight again, just eased back towards the bowler.
Boult comes back into the attack and starts off the new spell with a full and straight one. Shepherd drives it through wide mid on and thinks about two but settles for the single.
Odean Smith is in at number 9.

OUT! LBW! Ish Sodhi comes back strongly after getting hit for a couple of boundaries in the over and picks up his first wicket of the game. This is on a length and off, it is the wrong 'un. Rovman Powell tries to defend it off the front foot but misses and gets pinged on the pads. There is a huge appeal for LBW and it is given. Rovman Powell though reviews it straightaway. UltraEdge shows that no bat is invloved and Ball Tracking shows that the ball is hitting the top of middle stump. Powell has to walk back.
FOUR! Loops it up, full and wide, driven powerfully all along the ground and through extra cover for a boundary.
Nicely bowled! This is flighted, full and around off, Powell looks to slog sweep but pulls out at the last moment.
Drops it a bit short now but Shepherd mistimes the lofted pull shot over mid-wicket and collects a single.
Quicker and flatter, around middle and leg, Shepherd looks to flick off the back foot but misses and gets hit on the pads.
SIX! Easy power from Romario Shepherd! Flighted, around off and turning away, Shepherd stands tall and hits it with the turn, smoking it a long way over the wide long off fence.

Brilliant effort in the dep but lands just short. This is back of a length and angling into the body. Shepherd pulls it hard and flat towards deep square leg. Michael Bracewell comes in and puts in the dive but the ball lands just short and the batters get a run.
Length again, around off and punched out on the off side.

DROPPED! A difficult chance but Trent Boult completely misses it in the end. Length ball, around middle, Romario Shepherd looks to launch it over the mid-wicket fence but gets a top edge. The ball goes a long way up and is swirling around the third man region. Trent Boult over there runs towards it but misjudges it. The batters get a couple of runs.
Good length, around middle, this is worked away through mid-wicket for a run.
SIX! Just helped on its away. This is short and down the leg side, Rovman Powell uses the pace of the ball and pulls it over the fine leg fence for a maximum.
Southee starts off the new spell with a length ball, around middle and leg. This is pushed away to the right of the bowler for a single.
Flatter delivery on off, Rovman Powell keeps it out on the leg side off the back foot.
Around off, pushed away towards cover.
On a nagging length this time, around off, Powell eases it towards cover-point.
A tad shorter and this is played off the back foot towards backward square leg for a single.
Slower and shorter, outside off and turning away, Powell reaches out and gets an inside edge past leg stump for another single.
On a length and on middle and leg, Shepherd goes deep in his crease to push it towards long on for a run.
Mitchell Santner is back on.
Length now, around off, Shepherd looks to cut from too close to the body and chops it towards cover for one more.
A good bumper now, bowled at a good pace and around off. Romario Shepherd just sways his head away from the line of the ball.
A low full toss, outside off, Powell can only manage to loft it over the jumping extra cover fielder for a single.
FOUR! Wrong line from Boult and Rovman Powell punishes him. This is banged in short and over leg stump, Powell muscles it over short fine leg and finds the fence.
WIDE! An attempted slower delivery, spilled well down the leg side. Wided.
Length again, around the top of off, Shepherd nudges it towards mid-wicket for a quick run.
This is on a good length and angling in from outside off, Rovman Powell dabs it down to third man for a single.
Trent Boult (1-0-4-0) is back on.
At the stumps, Romario Shepherd blocks it out. Michael Bracewell ends his spell with figures of, 4-1-15-3!
Quicker and on middle, this is pushed down to long on for a single.

Drinks break! We are almost halfway through the chase and at the moment there seems to be no way back for West Indies. New Zealand bowlers have dominated and the Windies batters have had no answer. They are reeling at 40/6, needing 176 runs to win. it is only a matter of by how many runs the Kiwis win this contest. With that being said, Romario Shepherd walks out to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! Martin Guptill with a very well-taken catch and West Indies lose their sixth wicket! A tad shorter from Michael Bracewell, around middle and Jason Holder goes after it. Holder tries to lift it over long on but only manage to get the height, not the ditance. The ball is skied up around the mid on region and three fielders converge towards it. Martin Guptill comes in from long on and calls it before safely puching it. Michael Bracewell picks up his third wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Martin Guptill b Michael Bracewell

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter delivery, on off, this is worked away off the back foot through mid-wicket for a run.
Powell tries to use his feet but Bracewell sees him coming and pulls back the length. Powell keeps it out off his pads.
Full and straight, driven through wide mid on for a single.
Nicely flighted, full and around off, Rovman Powell fails to get it away.
Around off again, Powell pushes it towards cover and looks for the single but Holder says no.
Tossed up, around off and stroked away through covers for just another single.

This is the wrong 'un, turning in from around off. Rovman Powell tries to get inside the line of the ball and paddles it towards short fine leg for a single. There is an appeal for LBW from the bowler but it is turned down. Kane Williamson does review it after a bit of thought. The third umpire checks the UltraEdge first and there is indeed a slight under edge on it. The on-field decision of NOT OUT will stay.
Flatter delivery, outside off, this is tapped towards cover-point for one.
SIX! Sodhi drops it a bit short and Jason Holder latches onto it in a flash. Holder pulls it a long way over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
On middle, driven through mid on for a single.
BEATEN! On a length and close to the off stump, this one justn goes straight on and beats the outside edge of Holder's bat.
Rovman Powell is the new man in.

OUT! RUN OUT! An outstanding piece of fielding from Kane Williamson and West Indies lose yet another wicket. Around off, Shimron Hetmyer just bunts it out towards cover and tries to steal a single. Williamson runs to his right from extra cover and throws it at the bowler's end while falling over. Williamson gets in the direct hit and the replays show that Hetmyer is well short of his crease. New Zealand is total command here.

Is that run-out? Kane Williamson scores a direct hit at the bowler's end and the Kiwis are celebrating. The third umpire is called in. The replays show that Shimron Hetmyer is short of his crease and OUT is the decision.
Nicely tossed up, around off and driven straight towards cover.
SIX! This is shorter and around middle, Shimron Hetmyer uses the depth of the crease and pulls it well in front of mid-wicket for a flat six.
Quicker delivery, on off stump and just sliding on with the arm. Shimron Hetmyer shows quick hands as he manages to tap it towards point.
On off stump, Holder blocks it out.
On the pads, this is just worked away through square leg for a single.
Flatter delivery, around off, Holder goes back in his crease and just dabs it behind point for one more.
A tad shorter and around leg stump, Shimron Hetmyer goes on the back foot and flicks it towards fine leg for a single.
Here comes the wrong 'un, around off and turning away, Hetmyer does well to push it out on the off side.
Sodhi starts off his spell with a shortish delivery, Hetmyer though can't get it away.
Jason Holder is the new man in.

OUT! LBW! Devon Thomas has been pinged on the pads and in front of the stumps and has to walk back. Thomas pre-meditates and tries shuffle across the off stump. Michael Bracewell sees this and fires it in on a length and around middle. Thomas misses the paddle and gets cramped for room. The ball goes on to hit the pads. There is a loud appeal and the finger is raised. Thomas has a word with his partner but then just walks back.
Quicker and shorter, down the leg side, Thomas pulls it fine but finds the fielder at short fine leg.
Misfield and a single is taken. This is flatter, outside off and cut away straight towards point. The fielder over there fumbles and the batters get a run.
Some turn now! This is a bit shorter and around off, Hetmyer looks to pull off the back foot but the ball turns away and gets the toe end of the bat.
Full and around middle, Hetmyer flicks it uppishly towards mid-wicket. Sharp work from Mitchell Santner over there.
FOUR! That will ease the nerves for Shimron Hetmyer a bit. Short and wide, Hetmyer goes back and across before slapping it away through cover-point for a much-needed boundary.
On middle and leg, worked away in front of mid-wicket for one.
Thomas is finally able to get off the mark! This is sliding onto the pads, Thomas goes deep in his crease and flicks it behind square on the leg side for a single.
BEGTEN! Flighted delivery, nicely looped up outside off, drawing the batter forward. Thomas looks to block but gets beaten past the outside edge.
On a length, on off, Devon Thomas wrists it towards mid-wicket.
Flatter this time from Santner, around off, Thomas stays back and taps it towards backward point.
Floated up, around off and Thomas just eases it towards cover.
A wicket-maiden! This is flatter and around off, Hetmyer hangs back and taps it towards short third man.
Around off, pushed towards covers but can't find the gap.
Fired in on middle and leg, Shimron Hetmyer nudges it leg side.
Flatter again and outside off, Hetmyer punches it towards cover.
Quicker and flatter, outside off, Hetmyer looks to cut but misses.
Shimron Hetmyer is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Michael Bracewell now comes into the attack and strikes first ball too! New Zealand just ripping through the Windies' batting order here. Bracewell starts off with a bit of a long hop, well outside off and Nicholas Pooran goes chasing after it. pooran gets an under edge on it and it is a very sharp take from the wicket-keeper Devon Conway behind the sticks. The skipper departs early too and West Indies really struggling here.
Commentary.Howout: c Devon Conway b Michael Bracewell

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted, around off and kept out by Thomas. End of an excellent first over by Santner, just one run and two wickets off it.
Devon Thomas is the new man in.

OUT! TAKEN! Glenn Phillips takes a brilliant outfield catch and Mitchell Santner strikes twice in his first over. This is shorter and angled onto middle, Kyle Mayers rocks back and pulls it away. Mayers hits it flat and in front of mid-wicket. Phillips comes racing in from the deep and dives forward to grab it both hands just before the ball touches the ground. Mayers departs for a low score and West Indies in a spot of bother here.
Commentary.Howout: c Glenn Phillips b Mitchell Santner

Commentary.Commentary: A tad shorter and on the pads, Nicholas Pooran works it 'round the corner and gets off the mark with a single.
Slower again and around off, kept out by Pooran.
Santner switches to over the wicket and slows it up, on a length, turning it into off stump. Pooran looks to work it leg side but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
The skipper, Nicholas Pooran is in at number 3.

OUT! CLEANED HIM UP! Just like in the last game, Mitchell Santner strikes first ball! This is on a nagging length and around off, Shamarh Brooks backs away and gets down low. Brooks has a wild swing across the line but misses the line off the ball. The ball just slides on and goes on to crash into the off pole. Brooks departs early and West Indies on the back foot very early in the innings.
A change in bowling straightaway as Mitchell Santner has been handed the ball.
Switches to around the wicket for the finally delivery and angles in a length ball into middle. Mayers looks to hang back and nudge it leg side but misses and gets hit high on the pads.
Southee pushes this one wider and bowls it a touch fuller, Kyle Mayers goes after it but gets no connection whatsoever.
Excellent running! Around the top of off, just pushed towards mid on for a quick single.
FOUR! Dismissive from Brooks. Length ball, on off, Brooks stands tall and just lifts it back over the bowler's head. The ball almost goes the distance but pitches in front of the ropes.
This is angled onto the pads, Brooks clips it away past square leg for a couple of runs and he too is off the mark.
Southee starts off with a good-length delivery, angling it into the body. Shamarh Brooks hangs back and looks to work it leg side but misses and gets hit on the body.
Tim Southee to operate from the opposite end.
A bit shorter and around the hips, Mayers pulls it straight to the man at short fine leg.

FOUR! Up and over! Kyle Mayers gets his innings underway with a boundary. Length again from Boult, a touch fuller and outside off. Mayers drives it over extra cover and picks up the boundary. West Indies are off the mark with that as well.
Excellent delivery from Boult and equally well played. This is a yorker, on middle and Mayers does well to keep it out.
Swing and a miss! Good length, close to the off pole. Once again there's no feet movement from Mayers as he tries to hit through the line of the ball but misses.
Length again and there's some width on offer too as Boult falls over in the follow-through. Mayers though hits it straight towards cover.
Boult starts off with a length ball outside off, trying to swing it away. Kyle Mayers stays put and looks to drive but gets an under edge towards the keeper.
